_note: Human decisions about AMT substance -> RxNorm ingredient, for rows scripts/rxnorm_resolve.py could not resolve. Read by scripts/rxnorm_review_queue.py so that improving the resolver never discards a review, exactly as reference/binding_corrections.json does for SNOMED bindings.

_states.corrected_pending_attestation: a reviewer chose this concept; awaiting named sign-off
_states.attested: signed off by a named person; carries attestor and date
_states.rejected: this substance must NOT map to this concept

_vocabulary: OMOP Athena bundle v20260829; every target below was checked to be standard_concept=S and invalid_reason=NULL at decision time.

decisions.why: Pure taxonomic rename. Lactobacillus rhamnosus was reclassified to Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus in the 2020 split of the Lactobacillus genus (Zheng et al.); the organism is unchanged. RxNorm carries no valid species-level 'Lactobacillus rhamnosus' ingredient -- only strain-level RxNorm Extension entries (HN001, SP1, R0011, CLR2) -- so the renamed species concept is the only correct species-level target.
decisions.evidence: Athena: 100278 Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus, RxNorm, Ingredient, standard=S, invalid=NULL. AMT product terms name the plain species with no strain, so a strain-level target would be an unjustified narrowing.

decisions.why: B. lactis is a subspecies of B. animalis (Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis). RxNorm retired its own 'Bifidobacterium lactis' concept and points it at the species.
decisions.evidence: RxNorm's own deprecation decides this, not inference: concept 40242566 'Bifidobacterium lactis' (rxcui 1150094) has invalid_reason=U and carries both 'Concept replaced by' and 'Maps to' -> 45776867 Bifidobacterium animalis (standard=S, invalid=NULL). AMT product terms name no strain.

decisions.why: The resolver's candidate was WRONG and is rejected here. It offered 100272 'Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus', which narrows a species to one of its subspecies. L. delbrueckii has other subspecies (delbrueckii, lactis, indicus), and nothing in AMT says which is in these products.
decisions.evidence: All three AMT products name the plain species: 'Lactobacillus delbrueckii 250 million CFU' in a ten-organism capsule, its medicinal-product parent, and Probiotica (Nutra-Life) capsule. No AMT substance anywhere mentions bulgaricus or any delbrueckii subspecies (checked the whole substance table). Species-level target 40798917 is standard=S, invalid=NULL.

rejected_candidate.name: Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus
rejected_candidate.why_rejected: narrows species to subspecies without evidence

decisions.why: Genus-level match, recorded for completeness rather than benefit. The resolver found no candidate; RxNorm's retired genus concept points at this one.
decisions.evidence: Athena: deprecated RxNorm 6204 'Lactobacillus' (concept 987128, invalid_reason=D) 'Maps to' -> 36118942 Lactobacillus, RxNorm Extension, standard=S, invalid=NULL.
decisions.caveat: This unblocks nothing real. The two 'products' behind this substance are AMT grouper concepts -- 'Lactobacillus only product' and 'Lactobacillus-containing product' -- not marketed goods. The row is arguably a substance grouper and could instead be classed not-applicable; it is recorded as decided so it stops consuming review attention either way.
decisions.trap: Do NOT use 1147374 'Lactobacillus sp'. In this Athena bundle it is invalid (U) and both 'Concept replaced by' and 'Maps to' send it to 1310844 Bacillus coagulans, a different organism. Anything resolving genus-level Lactobacillus by following OMOP mappings blindly will land there.

decisions.why: The only contrast row that unblocks real marketed goods. AMT names the acid; the marketed form is the meglumine salt, and RxNorm models these products with the salt as the ingredient.
decisions.evidence: All 23 AMT products are Clariscan or Dotarem 0.5 mmol/mL injection (branded clinical drugs and their clinical-drug parents), both of which are gadoterate meglumine. Athena holds no 'gadoteric acid' ingredient and no bare 'gadoterate' — 1421151 gadoterate meglumine (RxNorm, standard=S, invalid=NULL) is the only candidate at any level.

decisions.why: Acid to anion, the standard RxNorm modelling for this agent. RxNorm carries no 'gadoxetic acid'.
decisions.evidence: Athena: 802624 gadoxetate, RxNorm, standard=S, invalid=NULL. Matches the resolver's candidate 1.
decisions.caveat: Unblocks nothing real: all four AMT products are abstract medicinal-product groupers ('Gadoxetic acid', 'only product', '-containing product in parenteral dose form'), not marketed goods.

decisions.why: The resolver's candidate is rejected. It offered 52527 'meglumine iotroxinate', the meglumine salt, when an exact acid-form ingredient exists and AMT names the acid.
decisions.evidence: Athena: 36854198 IOTROXIC ACID, RxNorm Extension, standard=S, invalid=NULL — an exact name match for the AMT substance. The salt would assert a formulation AMT does not state.
decisions.caveat: Unblocks nothing real: all four AMT products are abstract medicinal-product groupers.

rejected_candidate.name: meglumine iotroxinate
rejected_candidate.why_rejected: salt form asserted where AMT names only the acid, and an exact acid concept exists

decisions.why: Amidotrizoic acid (INN) and diatrizoic acid (USAN) are the same molecule, 3,5-diacetamido-2,4,6-triiodobenzoic acid. The resolver offered the anion; the acid itself exists and matches what AMT names.
decisions.evidence: Athena: 45775324 diatrizoic acid, RxNorm, standard=S, invalid=NULL. The resolver's candidate 3319 'diatrizoate' is the anion and is also standard, but is a less exact correspondent.
decisions.caveat: Unblocks nothing real: all four AMT products are abstract medicinal-product groupers. Note the related AMT substance 395875009 Sodium amidotrizoate already reaches OMOP and is not in the queue.

rejected_candidate.name: diatrizoate
rejected_candidate.why_rejected: anion where AMT names the acid and an exact acid concept exists

decisions.why: Iodised oil is ethiodised oil (Lipiodol); British and US spellings of the same preparation. Resolver candidate 1 and the legacy value agree.
decisions.evidence: Athena: 19050016 ethiodized oil, RxNorm, standard=S, invalid=NULL. The blocked product is Lipiodol Ultra-Fluid 10 mL (iodine 4.8 g)/10 mL injection; two of the three products already reached OMOP.

decisions.why: Not a substance. This is a pharmacological class and must not be mapped to an RxNorm ingredient; it belongs with the 370 rows already classified as substance groupers.
decisions.evidence: Its single ingredient row points at product 1144611009, which is not present in the product table at all — so even the count of 1 is a dangling reference, not a good.
